results: 1. Detailed ocular motility examination with cover–uncover and alternate-cover testing
ocular motility examination: bilateral limitation of abduction, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
2. Complete neurologic examination, including gait, heel walking, toe walking, tandem gait, and Romberg testing
cranial nerve examination: bilateral abduction limitation, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
limb strength (MRC) examination: mild distal limb weakness
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: reduced or absent reflexes; flexor plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): distal loss of vibration and proprioception
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
3. Examination for ocular and limb fatigability, including sustained upgaze and repetitive movements
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
5. MRI of the brain and orbits with gadolinium contrast
MRI orbits: normal extraocular muscles, no mass
MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
10. Thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine levels
11. Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin and thyroid peroxidase antibodies
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) with extensive bilateral cranial-nerve involvement, an autoimmune demyelinating neuropathy

ALTERNATIVE: Miller Fisher syndrome, an acute anti-GQ1b–associated Guillain–Barré variant

ALTERNATIVE: Neurosarcoidosis causing hypertrophic leptomeningeal and multiple cranial neuropathy involvement

ALTERNATIVE: Leptomeningeal lymphoma or carcinomatous meningitis with multiple cranial-nerve infiltration
